R0919.summary: Martina Lačoková is a Senior Research Associate in Computing and Control Engineering whose work centers on software testing, formal methods, and dependable embedded systems, especially for automotive and industrial CAN-based integration. Her record shows sustained expertise in combinatorial interaction testing, contract-based specification and verification, runtime monitoring, and tool-supported integration testing for multi-supplier embedded software.

Runtime verification and monitoring for CAN/CAN FD embedded systems

Tool-supported contract synthesis, benchmark construction, and incremental test maintenance

R0995.summary: Veljko Pantelić (R0995) is an Assistant Professor in Computing and Control Engineering whose work centers on software engineering for industrial automation, especially model-driven engineering for PLC software, DSLs, and product-line variability management. His record shows sustained work on IEC 61131-3 Structured Text tooling, code generation pipelines, safety-aware modeling, and evaluation benchmarks, with additional evidence of experience in industrial automation and PLC-related software development.

Software product lines and variability management for PLC systems
Domain-specific language design and code generation
Safety-aware and benchmark-driven industrial automation software engineering

C003-CH2.summary: AutomVoj a.d. is a Zrenjanin-based robotics and industrial automation company focused on conveyor and sorting systems for food and beverage producers. It has 212 employees and delivers PLC-based systems across Serbia and several Central European markets, with mechanical design, electrical assembly, PLC programming, and commissioning done in-house.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on plain-language explanations for automated micro and small business credit decisions at Kredo Fintech
proposal.problem: Kredo Fintech needs a compliant explanation format for its automated credit decisions that a borrower can understand and, if they wish, challenge. The current gradient-boosted model performs well, but the existing SHAP-based internal summary is too technical for borrowers and not yet suitable for production use in Serbian and Macedonian. The solution must be generated automatically at decision time, stored with the decision record, and work reliably in the borrower portal before expansion to North Macedonia.
research_questions: Which explanation template best preserves the key decision factors while remaining understandable to Serbian micro and small business borrowers in plain language?
How accurately can a decision-time explanation system map model features to compliant borrower-facing reasons without reducing underwriting performance or operational reliability?
How well does the same explanation design transfer from Serbian to Macedonian while keeping content consistent, readable, and auditable?

plan.work: Map the current decision pipeline at Kredo Fintech, review the existing SHAP-based internal summary, and define the explanation output schema needed for decision-time generation, storage, and portal display. Build a first Serbian prototype using the company’s existing Python, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, Airflow, scikit-learn, and REST API stack.
plan.result: A working Serbian prototype that generates explanation text and stores it with the decision record in a test environment.
plan.pass_if: At least 95% of test decisions receive an automatically generated Serbian explanation within the target decision workflow, and the explanation is stored with the decision record in the test pipeline.

plan.work: Run readability and compliance review with Kredo Fintech staff, including the compliance officer Dragana Vukić, and compare plain-language templates against the current technical summary. Refine the mapping from model drivers to borrower-facing reasons and test whether explanations remain stable across similar applicants.
plan.result: A revised Serbian explanation format that is clearer, more consistent, and ready for pilot testing.
plan.pass_if: Borrower-facing explanation drafts reach at least a 70% comprehension score in a small internal or borrower test set, and compliance review confirms that the output can be interpreted as challengeable in plain language.

plan.work: Pilot the explanation generator in the production-like environment, then check transfer to Kredo Fintech’s own portal and decision records. Begin the Macedonian version and verify that the same explanation logic can be rendered in both languages without breaking decision-time generation.
plan.result: A production-ready Serbian explanation workflow and a validated Macedonian translation workflow for the next expansion cycle.
plan.pass_if: The system generates and stores explanations at decision time with no blocking production errors during pilot testing, and the Macedonian version passes an agreed internal transfer check on Kredo Fintech’s own platform before any live use is claimed.

proposal.company_brings: Kredo Fintech brings a live automated lending workflow, its gradient-boosted scoring model, existing SHAP-based internal summaries, the borrower portal, and access to the decision records and operational constraints needed to design and test a compliant explanation format. The company also brings its in-house data team of five and its stack built on Python, dbt, Snowflake, Apache Airflow, scikit-learn, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, and Docker.
proposal.faculty_brings: Branislav Žarković brings expertise in credit scoring for thin-file borrowers, explainable credit risk models, alternative data, and regulatory aspects of lending, supported by his prior work on micro-enterprise scoring, explainability, and EU AI Act implications. The Faculty of Economics in Subotica brings industrial PhD supervision and research methods for designing, evaluating, and validating borrower-facing explanation formats.
proposal.why_this_pair: This pair combines a lender that must ship a compliant explanation solution in production within about six months with a researcher whose published work directly addresses explainable credit decisions, alternative data, thin-file borrowers, and regulatory expectations. The company’s real decision pipeline and the researcher’s credit-risk and explainability expertise fit the same problem at the right level of practical urgency.
proposal.novelty: The closest prior work is SYN-PUB-08747, "Explaining credit decisions to supervisors: a case study," which focuses on explaining credit decisions to supervisors rather than to borrowers. This project goes beyond that by designing, testing, and embedding a plain-language, decision-time explanation format for micro and small business borrowers, with dual-language deployment in Serbian and Macedonian and storage alongside the decision record. It also extends the researcher’s prior work in SYN-PUB-08751 and SYN-PUB-08754 by moving from explainability requirements and interpretability metrics to an operational, production-ready borrower communication workflow.
proposal.data_status: Kredo Fintech states that it already has an automated credit-scoring stack, a gradient-boosted ensemble model, SHAP-based feature attributions, decision records, borrower portal infrastructure, and a data team of five. The challenge text does not state that a borrower-tested plain-language explanation dataset already exists. To complete the project, the company would need to provide historical decision records, model outputs, SHAP explanations, portal rendering logs if any exist, and a sample of borrower-facing language for testing and translation. New data to be collected would include comprehension feedback, readability test results, compliance review notes, and Macedonian-language validation samples.
proposal.first_step: In November 2026, hold a joint scoping session with Kredo Fintech’s data team and compliance officer Dragana Vukić to freeze the explanation output format, identify the exact decision fields to expose, and select the test set of historical decisions for the first prototype.
proposal.to_agree: Funding for the industrial PhD, including who pays the doctoral candidate and any faculty supervision costs; the scope of access to historical decision records, model outputs, and portal logs; IP ownership and licensing for any new explanation templates, software code, and translation assets; publication delay for confidential results; approval rights for any borrower-facing wording; and data access rules for Serbian and Macedonian testing.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on contract-aware integration testing for multi-supplier CAN stacks at DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.
proposal.problem: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. reports 87% branch coverage and still sees CAN communication faults after delivery: in the last four delivered projects, three returned with integration bugs at boundaries between components from different suppliers. The company has ARXML descriptions, COM configuration, and CANoe, but no systematic way to generate tests that target the assumptions each side makes about the other. The research problem is to turn those artifacts into contract-aware integration tests that reveal cross-supplier interface faults before shipping, without disturbing the company’s AUTOSAR Classic process or customer toolchains.
research_questions: Can interface contracts be inferred from ARXML and COM configuration well enough to generate tests that expose cross-supplier CAN boundary faults better than the current spec-reading approach?
Which contract-aware combinatorial test strategy gives the best fault yield under the company’s practical constraint of not exceeding the first-phase budget of €40,000?
How accurately can the generated tests reproduce the kinds of interaction faults seen in the company’s last four delivered projects, while preserving the current 87% to 89% branch-coverage baseline?

plan.work: Collect one or two representative AUTOSAR/CAN integration cases from DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o., model the existing interface assumptions from ARXML and COM configuration, and adapt the researcher’s contract and combinatorial-test methods to the company’s CANoe-based environment. Prepare a prototype generator and check that it transfers to the company platform, not only the university laboratory setup.
plan.result: A working prototype that produces candidate contract-aware integration tests on the company’s own AUTOSAR/CANoe toolchain for at least one representative project.
plan.pass_if: The prototype reads the selected ARXML and COM inputs and generates at least 20 executable test scenarios; at least 80% of them run in CANoe without manual rewriting, and at least one scenario is accepted by the company as a realistic boundary-fault probe.

plan.work: Extend the prototype to cover multiple supplier boundary patterns, rank generated tests by likely interaction risk, and compare them with the company’s current integration tests on historical fault cases and a held-out project. Measure whether the new tests find faults earlier or with fewer tests than the current approach.
plan.result: A validated test-generation method with quantified fault-detection results on company-relevant cases.
plan.pass_if: On a held-out case, the new method finds at least one interaction fault missed by the company’s current test selection, while keeping generated test volume within the same order of magnitude as the current integration suite; if no new fault is found, the method must still match the current suite’s fault-revealing power on all available historical cases.

plan.work: Harden the method into a repeatable workflow for DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o., document how it fits into their AUTOSAR integration process, and add a transfer check for use on their own customer environments. plan.result: A company-ready workflow and research results suitable for dissertation writing and publication.
plan.pass_if: The workflow is usable by a DriveLogic engineer with the company’s own tools and data on a new project without university intervention for the core generation step; the company confirms that the process fits its AUTOSAR Classic and CANoe constraints before any result is claimed for operational use.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on modular reuse and safety patching for 38 divergent Siemens TIA Portal PLC codebases at AutomVoj a.d.
proposal.problem: AutomVoj a.d. has 38 active Siemens TIA Portal PLC codebases written in ladder logic that have drifted apart over time, so a safety-related patch such as an emergency stop sequence change currently takes three engineers two full weeks and still may not apply cleanly everywhere. The problem is to introduce a maintainable modular reuse approach that fits the company’s limited engineering capacity, does not require rewriting all systems at once, and can support safer, faster updates across the installed base.
research_questions: Can a reusable PLC software architecture be extracted from the 38 active codebases so that common safety-related logic can be standardized without full rewrites?

Can a migration and patching workflow be designed that reduces a typical safety patch from three engineers over two full weeks to a smaller, repeatable effort while preserving behavior on existing installations?

Can the proposed approach be transferred and tested on AutomVoj a.d.'s Siemens S7/TIA Portal environment and validated on representative conveyor-line cases without requiring a live installation change before safety review approval?

plan.work: Analyze a representative subset of the 38 codebases, identify shared patterns and variation points, and define a reusable modular structure for the most common safety and conveyor-control logic. Build a candidate library and an extraction/mapping method that fits Siemens S7-1500/S7-300 programming in TIA Portal.
plan.result: A validated modular reference architecture plus a first reusable library for selected logic families.
plan.pass_if: At least 10 codebases are analyzed; at least 3 recurring logic families are mapped into a reusable structure; and the first library can regenerate or support patches for at least 2 representative installations in the company environment.

plan.work: Develop incremental migration and patch application support so changes can be introduced without rewriting complete programs. Compare the new workflow against the current manual patch process on selected non-live examples from the 38 codebases.
plan.result: A repeatable patching workflow with measurable maintenance gains.
plan.pass_if: For at least 3 representative patch scenarios, the workflow reduces implementation effort below the current baseline of three engineers for two full weeks, while keeping the patched logic behavior equivalent on the tested examples.

plan.work: Harden the method for broader use across the installed base, document transfer steps for AutomVoj a.d. engineers, and evaluate maintainability, defect reduction, and adoption constraints. Prepare the doctoral thesis and publication package.
plan.result: A company-transferable method and documented adoption path for the installed base.
plan.pass_if: The approach is demonstrated on at least 5 additional codebases, a handover guide is accepted by the company, and the final evaluation shows that safety-related changes can be applied consistently across the tested set without live deployment before safety review approval.

proposal.company_brings: AutomVoj a.d. brings the real maintenance problem, the 38 active Siemens TIA Portal ladder-logic codebases, access to representative conveyor and sorting automation cases, and engineering knowledge from the company’s senior PLC staff. The company also brings its in-house testing environment in Zrenjanin, which is relevant for validation on its own Siemens S7-1500 and S7-300 platform.
proposal.faculty_brings: The Faculty of Technical Sciences brings Veljko Pantelić’s expertise in IEC 61131-3 metamodeling, model transformation, variability modeling, and PLC code generation, together with the academic environment, research methods, and small PLC laboratory with Wago and Beckhoff controllers for prototyping and controlled experiments.
proposal.why_this_pair: This pair fits because AutomVoj a.d. has a concrete and urgent maintenance bottleneck in PLC code reuse, while Veljko Pantelić has repeatedly worked on IEC 61131-3 Structured Text tooling, product-line variability, code generation, and safety-aware modeling. The company’s Siemens TIA Portal environment and the researcher’s experience in PLC software engineering create a direct route from method development to industrial validation.
proposal.novelty: The work goes beyond Veljko Pantelić’s closest prior publication, SYN-PUB-02958, by targeting extraction and reuse from already divergent ladder-logic codebases rather than incremental regeneration from an existing model. It also extends SYN-PUB-10379 by moving from extracting feature models from legacy PLC codebases to an end-to-end migration and patching workflow for safety maintenance in a live industrial setting. The novelty is the combination of reusable architecture extraction, incremental patch transfer, and company-specific validation on 38 active Siemens TIA Portal codebases.
proposal.data_status: The records state that AutomVoj a.d. currently has 38 active PLC codebases in Siemens TIA Portal, all written in ladder logic, and that one senior PLC programmer, Dragan Ilić, understands the full picture. The records do not state that a curated dataset, refactoring history, or labeled defect corpus already exists. The project would therefore need to collect a representative subset of codebases, document common patterns and variation points, record patch scenarios, and gather company feedback during validation. Any access to code and test environments must be agreed for the selected examples.
proposal.first_step: Next month, select a representative set of ladder-logic codebases with Dragan Ilić, inventory the most common safety and conveyor-control patterns, and agree on which 2 to 3 examples can be used first for analysis and transfer checking.
proposal.to_agree: Funding for the industrial PhD, who pays the candidate’s time, and how much company staff time AutomVoj a.d. can allocate beyond Dragan Ilić’s limited availability all need to be agreed. The parties also need to agree on background IP, ownership of new results, publication review delay, and the exact level of access to the 38 codebases, test benches, and documentation. Because the company uses Siemens TIA Portal on its own S7-1500 and S7-300 platform while the faculty lab uses different controllers, an explicit transfer check on AutomVoj a.d.'s platform must be agreed before any result is claimed for company use; for safety-related changes, nothing should run on a live installation until the company’s own safety review approves it.
